answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewal or negotiation can't meet the mandate this cycle. The contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so deferral risks a supply gap on a critical line already running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer—too risky given the objective to not increase delivery risk. The low-cost vendor quote alone meets the mandate, supporting a switch, but memory_c2's claim of quick onboarding and clean invoicing was recorded under different capacity conditions and should be verified before betting the primary line on it with no slack. Memory_c3 (second-sourcing) is worth checking because it may offer a lower-risk path to partially satisfy cost/resilience goals if a full primary switch proves too risky once verified. Given the zero-buffer constraint, I intend to switch primary supply but only as a small guarded test/parallel qualification run rather than a full cutover, preserving the option to fall back or add second-sourcing next cycle if the new vendor underperforms on delivery reliability.
